verdicts.claim: Checkpointing copies page changes from the WAL into the main database; when a page has multiple eligible versions, the latest relevant version is copied.
verdicts.evidence: Fly: "Checkpointing is when SQLite copies the latest version of each page in the WAL back into the main database file."

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint completion does not ordinarily imply that the physical WAL file shrinks; SQLite commonly reuses allocated WAL storage, while succes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning."

verdicts.claim: The standard automatic checkpoint threshold is 1000 pages, subject to compile-time or runtime configuration
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "threshold size of 1000 pages. (The SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT compile-time option ...)" plus wal_autocheckpoint pragma at runtime.

verdicts.claim: automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE and may remain incomplete
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "checkpoints initiated by ... the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE"; c3ref: "passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished".

verdicts.claim: RESTART additionally waits until readers use only the database file so the next writer can restart the WAL
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "blocks ... until all readers are reading from the database file only. This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning."

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE additionally reduces the WAL to zero bytes on successful completion
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: "it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return."

verdicts.claim: An active reader snapshot can limit checkpoint progress, and readers still using the WAL can prevent its reset; overlapping re
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound."

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: The WAL overview describes RESTART/TRUNCATE as ensuring completion ... busy handler that stops waiting can produce SQLI
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "...RESTART or ...TRUNCATE option which will ensure that the checkpoint runs to completion"; c3ref: "If the busy-handler returns 0 ... proceeds ... same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned".
